title: Deutsch’s algorithm
summary: One coherent query: turn equal or opposite signs into a measured bit.
why: The smallest exact coherent-query advantage exposes every amplitude and separates phase from probability.
advantage: Proven exact oracle separation: one coherent query versus two classical queries.

title: Grover’s algorithm
summary: Find one of four candidates by calculating a sign flip and reflection about the mean.
why: Four candidates let one full search iteration be calculated exactly, including its failure when repeated too long.
advantage: Proven quadratic query advantage for unstructured search; practical advantage not established by the toy instance.

title: Bernstein–Vazirani
summary: Recover a hidden parity string; follow every sign through three readout gates.
why: A structured parity function demonstrates recovery of several hidden bits with one coherent query.
advantage: Proven oracle separation: one quantum query versus order n classical queries.

title: Deutsch–Jozsa
summary: Test a constant-or-balanced promise, then deliberately break it.
why: A promise problem makes the exact-versus-randomized classical baseline distinction unavoidable.
advantage: Exponential exact deterministic oracle separation; no exponential advantage over bounded-error randomized sampling.

title: Simon’s algorithm
summary: Equal-output pairs produce random parity constraints; finish with classical elimination.
why: Equal-output pairs introduce entanglement, repeated Fourier samples, and classical equation solving.
advantage: Proven exponential bounded-error oracle-query separation for the promised unstructured oracle.

title: Synthesis: connect the mechanisms
summary: Trace the shared calculations without erasing their different access models, outputs, and costs.
why: Turn the curriculum into a way to analyze an unfamiliar quantum algorithm.
advantage: No new advantage claim: connects earlier proved, conditional, and heuristic results without conflating their models.
